title: Creating Tensor Maps
author: Courtney Comrie
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8jyhupw
materials: Select Next in the lower right hand corner.
Once you have added enough "bubbles" select next.
Type the following: EstimateTensorNLSS -i directory_DRBUDDI_proc/file_name.list -m directory/mask_name.nii
Choose your display mode to be RGB Display.
Once you have added enough "bubbles" select next.

steps.title: Launch ITK‑SNAP via Singularity
steps.instruction: Open a terminal, change to the container directory, load the Singularity module, and run the ITK‑SNAP container.

steps.title: Load structural image
steps.instruction: In ITK‑SNAP, browse to the folder DTITest_DTI_proc_DRBUDDI_proc and open the file structural.nii.

steps.title: Create brain mask with snake tool
steps.instruction: Use the snake tool and related controls to segment the brain, adjust thresholds, grow bubbles, and save the mask as a NIFTI file.

substeps.instruction: Click the Snake tool to start mask creation.
Move the red lines to adjust boundaries for the fill function.
Select Segment 3D after adjusting the red lines.
Select the blue thresholding view and adjust the threshold until bone, muscle tissue, and eyes are removed as desired.
Click the Add Bubble at Cursor button while clicking around in all three orthogonal views to place seed points.
Press the Play button to grow the bubbles; optionally press the Update button to view the growing mask.
When satisfied, press the Pause button and then click Finish.
Press Update a second time to display the completed mask in the lower‑left corner.
Save the mask as a NIFTI file and exit ITK‑SNAP.

steps.title: Generate tensor estimation files
steps.instruction: Run EstimateTensorNLLS to obtain two output files, _DT.nii and _AM.nii; the _DT.nii file will be used for subsequent map creation.

steps.title: Compute all tensor maps
steps.instruction: Execute ComputeAllTensorMaps.bash with the path to the _DT.nii file to generate every available tensor map.

steps.title: Compute specific tensor map (DEC)
steps.instruction: If only a single map is required, run the appropriate command (e.g., ComputeDECMap) and replace ‘DEC’ with the desired map name for other maps.

substeps.instruction: ComputeDECMap -i directory/tensor_file_name.nii   // outputs a DEC map

steps.title: Visualize DEC map in ITK‑SNAP
steps.instruction: Open the generated DEC map in ITK‑SNAP, click the Layer Inspector button, and view the finished RGB display.

substeps.instruction: Click the Layer Inspector button to view the RGB overlay.
